correctness.rationale: The Finding specifies Paley column order with the Sylvester row sequence: the raw Sylvester binary column indices are bit-reversed for these displayed labels. With row r, column j, the unscaled entry is (−1)^popcount(r & reverse3(j)). Summing this product for two columns over 2^k prefix rows gives 2^k if their low k character bits match and zero otherwise, which is the stated consecutive-block condition in Paley labels. Bare Sylvester columns without the Paley reorder would relabel the listed optimizers. An independent exact checker computed these pairwise overlaps directly from signs, enumerated all 4^8 length assignments, and used rational symmetric Schur-complement pivots to test 68I−5H for strict positive definiteness. It found exactly the eight stated XOR vectors outside the bound; all other 65528 have squared norm strictly less than 17/10. Newton identities on exact traces gave t^4(t−4)(t^3−16t²+32t−16) for each exception. The exact signs q(68/5)=−3088/125 and q(14)=40 put a root above the separation, hence all exceptions have the common larger squared norm; t=8ζ transforms the top factor into the claimed cubic. Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/b602047d-6d27-4349-895a-5f6e56a17799/audit_record5.py (no --limit); full run in the adjacent full.log, with the eight vectors and all assertions checked. Uploaded verify.py inspected, not executed. The last displayed digit of the supplementary squared-norm approximation is off by about 1.1×10^−15 (the largest root begins 1.719840461515739140); the exact cubic, gap and correctly approximated norm are unaffected. This is exhaustive at size eight only.

value.rationale: This is a motivated finite benchmark of the published single-branch maximal-norm problem, not just a recomputation of its already motivated candidate polynomial. Quantifying every allowed column choice excludes alternative maximizing branch patterns and supplies strict quantitative separation, both facts a researcher testing a general branching comparison can use. The exhaustive result makes no claim about higher levels.
